messages:
olivia: Hey team — customer sent an export that downloads as a 0-byte CSV. They select a 90-day range and include 'raw_events'. Happens intermittently (~1/5 exports). Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4121. Payload: export_id=exp_9a2f4, account=acct_88. Can someone triage? :frowning_face:

sam: Thanks, can you paste the export job id + the presigned url from the support logs? Also which browser/os?

olivia: Job: exp_9a2f4. Support logs show presigned URL returned by export-service: `https://s3.redwood-internal/.../exp_9a2f4.csv?X-Amz-Signature=...` Server side log snippet:
```
2026-02-21T15:11:12.342Z export-service INFO upload-init job=exp_9a2f4 size_est=14MB presigned_url="..."
2026-02-21T15:11:13.019Z export-service INFO stream-start job=exp_9a2f4 rows=0
2026-02-21T15:11:13.133Z export-service WARN csv-writer aborted job=exp_9a2f4 reason=write error: write to s3 returned 200 with 0 bytes
```
User curl of presigned URL returns 200 but zero bytes:
```
curl -I "https://...exp_9a2f4.csv?..."
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 0
Content-Type: text/csv
```
They report other exports (same account) succeed. Browser: Chrome Mac, same 0-byte file.

tariq: Tagging eng. From the logs it looks like the service is returning a presigned URL as usual, but the stream to S3 ended early. We saw a deploy to export-service yesterday at 15:10 UTC. @eng-deploy-bot can you confirm the release?

eng-deploy-bot: deploy: export-service v1.12.3 -> production at 2026-02-21T15:09:58Z by ci/pipeline #4821 :rocket:

tariq: OK. Hypothesis: there's an encoding/streaming edge case when events contain embedded NUL (0x00) bytes or unescaped control chars. The CSV writer uses a buffered stream that treats some write errors as EOF and closes; S3 ends up with a zero-length object when the multipart/put is aborted but presigned url still points to an empty key.

sam: Any quick repro? Could we craft a small export that includes an event with a NUL?

olivia: I grabbed a problematic event from the customer: payload contains embedded null bytes in base64-decoded trace. Repro script (local):
```python
import requests
from io import BytesIO
# simulate event with null byte
s = "id,body\n1,hello\x00world\n"
open('test.csv','wb').write(s.encode('utf-8'))
# upload using same client lib we use to stream to s3 - shows same truncation locally
```

tariq: Nice repro, thanks. Quick mitigation: force CSV writer to sanitize control chars and replace NULs before writing to the stream. That will avoid the internal write path that currently returns early. I can prepare a patch. Also adding extra validation on multipart uploads so we don't leave 0-byte objects.

support-ops: Customer wants ETA, impact is 3 exports in last 24h across 2 customers. Any temporary workaround we can give them?

tariq: Workaround for support: ask customer to uncheck 'include raw_events' or select a shorter time range. If they must have raw events, ask them to run exports via the API and use our documented retry (we have a client-side retry that will fetch again on 0-byte). I'm going to open an internal PR for the sanitizer + upload integrity check.

sam: Please paste the PR link when ready. Also, can we add an alert to SRE for zero-byte object creations under the exports bucket? That would catch this earlier.

tariq: Will do. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/export-service/pull/2098 (WIP) — adds NUL stripping and upload-complete verification. Plan: hotfix to v1.12.4 rollback if needed.

olivia: Added note to ticket CS-4121 with the workaround and ETA for patch (ETA 6 hours). Customer acknowledged and will try the shorter-range workaround. :white_check_mark:

support-ops: Great, please keep me posted. If you want me to escalate to enterprise CSM let me know.

tariq: I'll ping when PR is merged and new image is deployed. Also adding a unit test to stream a payload with \x00 to prevent regressions.

olivia: Thanks everyone — I'm marking this thread as tracked in the ticket.
